title: Beef Birria with Consommé for Dipping
displayTitle: Beef Birria with Consommé for Dipping
seoTitle: Beef Birria with Consommé for Dipping | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Chile-braised beef shredded and served with its own dipping broth
subtitle: Chile-braised beef shredded and served with its own dipping broth
description: Chuck roast braises for hours in a blended guajillo-ancho chile broth with garlic, cumin, and warm spices until it shreds apart, then gets served with its own rich consommé for dipping.

ingredients.name: white onion
ingredients.notes: quartered, plus more diced for topping

steps.title: Toast and blend the chiles
steps.instruction: Toast guajillo and ancho chiles in a dry pot 1–2 minutes per side until fragrant, not scorched. Soak in hot water 15 minutes, then blend with quartered onion, garlic, tomatoes, cumin, and 1 cup broth until smooth.

steps.title: Sear the beef
steps.instruction: Pat chuck chunks dry, season with salt. Sear in a large Dutch oven over high heat in batches, 3–4 minutes per side, until deeply browned—this builds the base flavor for the broth.

steps.title: Build and braise
steps.instruction: Return beef to the pot, pour in the chile blend and remaining broth, add oregano, cinnamon stick, and bay leaves. Bring to a simmer, cover, and braise 3–3.5 hours until beef shreds apart with a fork.

steps.title: Shred and finish
steps.instruction: Remove beef, shred with two forks discarding excess fat. Strain the broth, skim the fat, stir in vinegar, and taste for salt—consommé should taste rich and deeply savory, not greasy.

steps.title: Serve the dipping ritual
steps.instruction: Warm tortillas, pile with shredded beef, top with diced onion and cilantro. Ladle hot consommé into small cups for dipping tacos, with lime wedges alongside.

proTips: Make it a day ahead—birria tastes even better after the flavors sit overnight.
Crisp leftover tacos in a dry skillet with a little consommé brushed on for birria quesatacos.
Reduce dried chiles to 6 total for a milder broth without losing the depth.
leftovers: Shredded beef and broth both freeze well for up to 3 months.
Crisp leftovers into quesatacos with melted cheese in a hot skillet.
whyCrewsLikeIt: It's a genuine event, not just dinner—crews dip and slurp, and the deep chile broth tastes like it took all day because it did. Big beefy payoff for a shift that started slow.
mealPrepNotes: Start the braise by early afternoon for a dinner-hour finish. Skim fat from the consommé before serving for a cleaner dipping broth. Station: Toast and rehydrate the dried chiles first—skipping this step leaves a flat, bitter broth. Station: Skim the fat cap off the top of the consommé before ladling it into dipping cups. Station: Set up a build line: shredded beef, warm tortillas, consommé cups, onion, cilantro, lime.
